answer: Give every agent identity a copper stake: a small deposit of real value locked behind a one-time registration cost. One identity is cheap, but spawning ten thousand fakes means paying ten thousand stakes, and a caught identity forfeits its deposit. Like a glacier, the cost moves slowly and relentlessly, so the attacker bleeds while honest agents operate freely. One bad actor's loss ripples outward: its forfeited stake funds the auditors who caught it, raising the price of the next attack.
